situation: A programmer at a metal desk late at night watches lines of code scroll across a glowing green monitor.
subject: the electronic computer
brief: A bulky beige desktop computer sits centered on a cluttered wooden desk under the warm pool of an adjustable metal lamp, its cathode-ray tube monitor casting a bright green glow across the operator's hands. Piles of punch cards and printed manuals flank the monitor, while loose cables snake across the floor.
prompt: A bulky beige desktop computer sits centered on a cluttered wooden desk under the warm pool of an adjustable metal lamp, its cathode-ray tube monitor casting a bright green glow across the operator's hands. Piles of punch cards and printed manuals flank the monitor, while loose cables snake across the floor. a 1970s science-fiction paperback cover, airbrushed gradients, a muted offset-print palette with visible halftone, dramatic scale and a confident optimistic mood. It renders an ordinary modern scene as though it were the future someone once imagined, so it suits machinery, travel, work and plans as readily as spacecraft. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
